newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate down to 10.4 pct from 11.3.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate down to 10.4 pct from 11.3.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate slumped to 10.4 percent in modest trade on Tuesday from 11.3 percent the previous day, as bank liquidity improved ahead of the monthly pension pay date.
The total daily trade halved to 24.5 million kuna, of which 13 million were fresh loans, mostly call money granted at a steady 10.5 percent rate.
One 1.5 million kuna interbank loan was granted at 11 percent.
Neither demand nor supply were fully met as lenders and borrowers failed to agree on terms.
Insurers rolled over previous one-week funds at steady nine percent. Banks extended old loans at 10 and 11 percent for one-week and 14 percent for three-week borrowings.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday weaker at 6.1681 against the dollar and 3.5732 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, 385-1-4557075
